headline: Iraq Sends 2 Million Barrels of Crude Through Strait of Hormuz
seoTitle: Iraq Sends 2 Million Barrels of Crude Through Hormuz | FMB News
seoDescription: Iraq's state tanker company says it moved 2 million barrels of crude through the Strait of Hormuz, its first such operation in decades.
deck: The state tanker company's first such operation in decades provides a new export option, but it does not establish that the wider shipping disruption has ended.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company said it transported 2 million barrels of Iraqi crude aboard a very large crude carrier through the Strait of Hormuz, describing the voyage as its first operation of that kind in decades.

Director General Ali Qais Abdul Jabbar said the company is carrying crude through the strait instead of ending its role at the port of Basra, giving state oil marketer SOMO more flexibility over where and how it sells the cargo.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Reuters reported the company statement at 8:24 p.m. UTC on October 3, or 4:24 a.m. Philippine time on October 4. Iran International separately reported the same two-million-barrel shipment and the company's description of it as its first such operation in decades.

Iraqi official records provide context for the voyage: the Oil Ministry said in March that it was seeking Iranian permission for Iraqi tankers to use the strait, and a September ministry clarification said Iraq was sustaining exports while the waterway remained disrupted.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: The company did not identify the vessel, loading and delivery ports, buyer, sale price or precise transit date in the public material reviewed by FMB News. Independent vessel-tracking confirmation of the specific cargo was not available in the sources reviewed.

One successful transit does not mean the Strait of Hormuz has fully reopened or returned to normal commercial traffic. Security risks, Iranian transit permissions and shipping costs remain separate questions.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The shipment is a new development in the Hormuz supply crisis. FMB News first reported on September 3 that U.S.-Iran tensions were threatening Gulf shipping and pushing oil prices higher: https://www.francinemariebautista.com/news/oil-six-week-high-us-iran-hormuz-september-3-2026/

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for Gulf oil and liquefied natural gas. Iraq previously relied mainly on export arrangements centered on Basra while seeking permission for selected tankers to pass through the strait.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The Philippines imports most of its petroleum requirements. Additional crude movement through Hormuz could help supply flexibility, but this single cargo is not evidence that diesel or gasoline prices will fall. Local effects depend on sustained flows, refining capacity, freight costs, exchange rates and subsequent oil-company price advisories.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for additional Iraqi tanker voyages, vessel-tracking confirmation, official SOMO sales disclosures, changes in Hormuz transit volumes and any effect on global crude and refined-product prices.

verificationNotes: The two-million-barrel figure and first-in-decades characterization are attributed to the Iraqi state company's director general.
Reuters and Iran International independently reported the state company announcement.
Iraqi official records corroborate the policy background that selected Iraqi tankers required transit permission and that the strait remained disrupted.
FMB News did not find independently reviewable vessel-tracking data for the specific cargo, so the voyage details remain attributed to the company.
The article does not treat one voyage as proof that Hormuz shipping has normalized or that Philippine fuel prices will decline.
The contextual photograph is a verified public-domain U.S. Navy work and is accurately labeled as a 2020 file image, not the 2026 Iraqi cargo.
